newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN GROWTH HOLDING GIMV IN STRONG BOURSE DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN GROWTH HOLDING GIMV IN STRONG BOURSE DEBUT.

text.p: Holding company GIMV, rated a growth stock by analysts, made a strong bourse debut on Thursday, rising well above its 2,010 franc IPO price.
GIMV stock opened at 2,100 francs to stand at 2,090 by 0930 GMT in volume of 135,937 shares.

Generale Bank said in its Belgian Equity Focus it estimated GIMV's net asset value at 2,381 francs per share. It expected the market to slap a lower discount to NAV on GIMV shares than on other, more traditional, holding companies.
"We would not be surprised by a discount of about 10 percent, so that the price could rise to about 2,150 francs."
Half of GIMV's portfolio consists of its stake in Belgian electronics group Barco , the rest of minority stakes in some 200 Flemish growth companies.
Other market watchers were less positive on GIMV.

"GIMV has some potential. But not that much...it has not come to the market cheap, taking up the trend of falling price discounts in relation to asset value seen recently for holdings," analyst Patrick Millecam at Corluy said.
Another analyst also said the GIMV issue price was on the expensive side.

The price had been calculated on the basis of the evolution of profit and shareholders' equity over the last three years -- a period in which GIMV had cashed in on some of its holdings through the sale of stakes and/or the listing of interests.
GIMV benefitted from the performance of Barco, Lernout & Hauspie, Xeikon and Innogenetics, he said.

He added that over a five to seven year period GIMV would not have done nearly as well. "It would not be a match for a holding like Gevaert , one of the better ones." He noted the recent fall in the share price discount of holdings to net asset value had been triggered by the split-up of Gevaert.
The bulk of Gevaert's assets have been divided up between holding companies Almanij and Cobepa .

The analyst did not see much of a chance for quick price rises at GIMV. He preferred other Belgian holding companies such as Tubize, Obourg , Moustier , GBL and Electrafina , which traded at a higher discount to asset value and had more potential for price gains in the current trend towards restructuring in the holdings sector.
Shares in Belgian holding companies often trade at discounts of 20 to 25 percent to net asset value per share.

At a ceremony in the Flemish parliament to mark the first day of trading in GIMV shares board chairman Rainier van Outryve d'Ydewalle said that he could not answer the often-posed question whether GIMV would be able to repeat past successes.

"GIMV is a long-term investor...this philosophy of being a patient investor corresponds to the characterictics of a growth share. Although the GIMV must be considered mainly as a growth stock, we will have a policy of regularly increasing our dividend, depending on inflation and GIMV's profits."
Brussels bourse director Olivier Lefebvre said GIMV's listing was the largest in a series of nine new listings in six months' time.
Flemish Economy Minister Eric Van Rompuy said the listing of GIMV, in which the Flemish government keeps a 70 percent stake, would boost the managerial autonomy and financing capacity of the holding.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
